subject: Private deployment: customer KMS handshake & data access boundaries
messages:
From: Julie Kim <julie.kim@acme-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-12 09:05 -0700
Subject: Private deployment questions: customer-managed keys and emergency access

Hi Evelyn / Jordan,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As we scope our Private deployment (VPC + on-prem connector) we have a few items the security team asked us to document before we proceed: 

- Confirmation that Acme will be able to retain exclusive control of the master key (KMS) and that Redwood will not have an automatic "operator" key.
- A short description of the handshake/authorization steps Redwood will perform if Acme's KMS signs a session token for the runtime.
- A clear matrix of roles that can access logs, model output, and KV caches (e.g., support_engineer vs. infra_ops vs. SRE).
- A few example incident scenarios where Redwood might request temporary investigative access and the escalation path (we need SLA for response + audit trail).

We attached a first-pass DPA redline and a diagram of the KMS handshake to speed the legal/security review. Let us know if you prefer a separate call with our InfoSec folks.

Best,
Julie
Julie Kim
Head of Security Ops, Acme Corp

Attachments: ACME_DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx), kms-handshake-diagram.pdf (pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
To: Julie Kim <julie.kim@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-06-12 11:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: customer-managed keys and emergency access

Hi Julie —

Appreciate the clear list and the attachments; those are perfect. Initial answers inline below, then a proposal for next steps.

1) Customer-exclusive master key: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS where the master key never leaves Acme's control. For our VPC/on-prem package we integrate via a mTLS endpoint + signed session tokens; Redwood does not hold an operator key by default. There are two optional exceptions (both require a signed SOW):
  - Disaster recovery escrow (customer opt-in) where an encrypted ephemeral keyshare is held in a sealed escrow HSM accessible only with multi-party authorization.
  - Short-term emergency access: only available with documented legal approval and an immutable audit record.

2) Handshake: high-level steps (we'll share a diagram):
  - Acme KMS issues a short-lived signed session credential (JWT) scoped to a specific runtime and validity window.
  - Runtime validates signature and request context (instance id, sequence, nonce) and establishes a TLS session bound to the credential.
  - Redwood enforces token scope (no cross-tenant reuse) and logs the handshake with timestamp, subject, and nonce.

3) Access matrix: By default, logs and model traces are encrypted at rest and segmented by tenant. Roles we typically expose:
  - support_engineer: can view request-level metadata and non-sensitive tracing (no decrypted customer plaintext).
  - infra_ops: can view instance health metrics and aggregated performance traces (no plaintext).
  - security_admin: can request decrypted artifacts only if a legal-approved audit or incident is authorized; every action creates an immutable audit trail.

4) Incident scenarios: we propose three levels with SLAs:
  - Info: non-sensitive issue — meeting within 48h, no data access needed.
  - Investigative: requires logs + scoped KV cache snapshot — access only with signed legal consent; Redwood response (prepare exports) within 24h; access audit posted to the customer.
  - Emergency (active breach): temporary access possible under Executive Escalation (see process), logged and revoked immediately after triage; we recommend a 2-hour response target for acknowledging the request.

Next steps: Jordan / Karthik — can you review the DPA redline and the handshake diagram Julie attached and propose any additions to the emergency access process? We can schedule a 30-min call with Acme InfoSec if they prefer.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Product (Security & Deployments)
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Julie Kim <julie.kim@acme-corp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-06-13 09:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: customer-managed keys and emergency access

Julie — thanks for the prompt. I reviewed the DPA redline and sketched a short "handshake responsibilities" appendix for clarity. Key points in the attached redline:

- We accept the customer-controlled KMS model as requested; we added a paragraph that forbids Redwood from performing any key import or export without a mutually signed SOW.
- Added explicit commit that access to decrypted model outputs requires a signed incident authorization form and will be limited to the minimum necessary scope.
- Clarified that audit logs are retained per the DPA retention schedule and that customers can request on-demand exports.

I attached the updated redline (ACME_DPA_redline_v1.1.docx) and a small diagram showing who signs what during the handshake.

Attachment: ACME_DPA_redline_v1.1.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Julie Kim <julie.kim@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-06-14 10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: customer-managed keys and emergency access

Thanks Jordan/Evelyn — helpful edits. A few clarifications legal/security will want included before we mark the DPA redline ready: 

- Subprocessor list: we need to enumerate third-party vendors who will have access to runtime telemetry (e.g., cloud provider logs, observability vendors). Please confirm the minimum subprocessor set for the VPC/on-prem pattern and whether any of them can decrypt customer data under any circumstance.
- Cross-border transfer: please add a clause stating that telemetry/audit exports related to an incident will be delivered to Acme's designated endpoint and will not be mirrored to other Redwood regions without consent.
- Temporary investigative snapshots: define retention period for any exported KV cache snapshot (default: 90 days unless customer requests shorter).
- Handshake replay prevention: confirm nonce/window settings and whether Redwood will persist handshake nonces for X days for forensic replay tests.

Julie — can you confirm the minimum set of subprocessors you expect to see (if Acme requires a narrow list we'll propose a minimal stack)? For next steps, would Acme prefer a short SOC/architecture session to run the personnel-level access matrix (support vs infra vs security_admin) with names?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product Security (Redwood Inference)

From: Julie Kim <julie.kim@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-06-14 16:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: customer-managed keys and emergency access

Thanks all — this is great progress.

Quick answers:
- Minimum subprocessors we expect: (1) cloud provider (us-west-2), (2) observability vendor (TraceLite), (3) SSO provider (Okta). None have decryption rights; they're limited to telemetry and encrypted metadata.
- Cross-border: confirmed — deliverables stay in-region unless we provide written consent.
- Retention: 90 days for investigative snapshots is acceptable; we may ask to shorten to 30d per LR, but can be negotiated per incident.
- Nonce retention: please retain handshake nonces for at least 180 days for forensic validation.

Let's schedule a 30-min technical call Monday to walk through the personnel access matrix (I will invite our InfoSec engineer). Can you share the updated redline (ACME_DPA_redline_v1.1) and the handshake diagram in the calendar invite?

-Julie
Julie Kim
Head of Security Ops, Acme Corp
